title: Bridge Room Corridor Notes — Week of Nov 16–22, 2026
content:
Context: quick notes captured in the bridge room and corridor after the weekly on-call rotation and today's mini-incident bursts. This is intentionally messy — friction log + handoff summary so next on-call has what they need.

Attendees / contributors (real-time): Marina (scribe), Ethan (lead), Sofia (metrics), Devinder (network), Mia (observability ping-in).

Week summary (one-liner): Two small, related incidents (prefix-cache thrash + regional throttling) caused elevated p50/p95 CPU on gpu-backends in us-west2 for ~45m; all user-facing errors were routed to fallback model variants with no customer-facing degradations, but cost spiked and several anomalous retries appeared.

Incident A — prefix-cache thrash (2026-11-17 14:12–14:48 UTC)
  - Symptoms: sudden increase in model-server CPU utilization and tail latency. Persistent 429s from model runtime to the routing layer; client retries grew 3x.
  - Trigger: long-running A/B job started by data-science (job DS-472) that performs long prefix scans, causing cache churn and poor KV hit rates.
  - Detection: anomaly alert from metrics pipeline (p95 token latency > 2x baseline) triggered paging to on-call.
  - Timeline:
    - 14:12: first alert fired (p95 <= 300ms baseline -> ~750ms)
    - 14:18: Ethan identified high cache miss rate (KV cache miss ratio spiked from 6% -> 48%)
    - 14:26: partial mitigation — throttled DS-472 via quota override and rolled back a recent model routing change (routing-policy-qa->prod) to reduce heterogeneity on hosts
    - 14:38: applied temporary prefix-rate-limit (edge) to DS job, observing gradual recovery
    - 14:48: system stabilized; left mitigations in place pending follow-up
  - Immediate follow-ups (short):
    - DS team to reconfigure DS-472 to use dedicated Dedicated pool or lower concurrency (owner: Priya, due 2026-11-20).
    - Ops to add a safety circuit: automatic prefix-rate-limit when KV miss rate > 30% for 5m (owner: Devinder, ticket SRE-388).
    - Note: consider increasing cold-KV-cache capacity or warming strategy for experimental jobs.

Incident B — regional throttling cascade (2026-11-18 03:07–03:25 UTC)
  - Symptoms: sudden increase in routing errors and fallbacks for requests routed to eu-west1-originated traffic. Fallback policy triggered to smaller, cheaper model variant for ~18 minutes.
  - Root cause hypothesis: noisy neighbor in dedicated pool in eu-west1 caused GPU overheating throttles on a subset of hosts, which then hit autoscaling/fallback churn.
  - Detection/response: automated fallback worked as designed; customer-facing latency remained within SLO but unit cost increased and error budget for that route consumed ~0.7%.
  - Follow-ups:
    - Infra to inspect dedicated pool thermal telemetry and host replacement cadence (owner: Noah, due 2026-11-22).
    - Add a routing policy heatmap to console for quicker region-heat detection (owner: Sofia, spike due 2026-11-25).

SLO snapshot (quick):
  - Serving API global availability (30d rolling): 99.97% (SLO 99.95%) — PASS
  - Per-route error budget consumption (last 7d): route-chat-west: 0.6% consumed, route-embeddings: 1.6% consumed (watching)
  - Token latency p95 (global): 380ms (target p95 < 400ms)
  - Note: Incident B consumed a small fraction of fallback allowance; net availability unaffected.

On-call handoff (to: on-call-week-2026-11-19)
  - Current mitigations in place to monitor: prefix-rate-limit rule temporary expression, DS-472 quota hold, eu-west1 pool watchlist.
  - Who to call: Ethan (runtime), Devinder (infra), Priya (DS owner), Noah (infra ops).
  - Tickets to track: SRE-388 (prefix safety circuit), SRE-389 (eu-west thermal inspection).
  - Suggested priorities for next shift:
    1) Implement and test prefix-rate-limit automation (high).
    2) Validate DS job scheduling guardrails and add a DS job runway policy for long-prefix scans (medium).
    3) Add region heatmap + thermal telemetry dashboard to console (medium).

Retro notes / open questions:
  - Why did DS job run on shared pool rather than sandbox? Is onboarding doc unclear or missing guardrails?
  - Can we simulate prefix-thrash in staging to validate circuit behavior? (note to self: Mia to help craft replay workload)
  - Should fallback policies include cost-guard rails (avoid expensive fallback route during peak to preserve budget)?

Action items (who / by when):
  - Devinder: implement automated prefix-rate-limit rule + unit tests (SRE-388) — ETA 2026-11-24
  - Priya (DS): move DS-472 to dedicated pool + lower concurrency — ETA 2026-11-20
  - Sofia: create region heatmap spike dashboard + alert (console-ticket) — ETA 2026-11-25
  - Noah: collect thermal logs and schedule host replacement if persistent — ETA 2026-11-22
  - Marina: write short post-incident blurb for ops channel + link to SRE tickets — ETA 2026-11-19

Notes to self (raw):
  - Watch interplay between KV cache size and model tokenization changes — some recent tokenizer updates may increase key cardinality.
  - Come up with a short playbook snippet: "When KV miss > X% and p95 > Y for > Z minutes -> apply prefix-rate-limit and escalate to DS"
  - Keep small list of allowed long-running DS jobs that must use dedicated capacity.

Random meeting fragments (copied from sticky):
  - "Can we detect long-prefix jobs before they start?" — think: admission hook or job label requirement.
  - "Fallback shaves cost but can mask root cause" — agree; need a paired alert to detect when fallback has been active > 10m.

Attachments / helpful links:
  - SRE-388 (ticket) — prefix safety circuit (linked above)
  - SRE-389 (ticket) — eu-west thermal inspection
  - PR: serving-runtime#2147 — hotfix that reduced cache eviction aggressiveness (deployed 2026-11-11)
  - Confluence: runbook draft under ops/runbooks/cache-eviction-policy (working copy)

Bottom line: routing + cache interactions caused transient thrash that our fallback and routing policies handled without customer impact. Need a few safety automations and DS guardrails to avoid repeated cost/noise. Handoff done.

-- Marina
